Title: PBM AND ACTIVATED SLUDGE FLOCCULATION: FROM EXPERIMENTAL DATA TO A CALIBRATED MODEL

Abstract: Abstract: A calibration methodology is presented for a Population Balance Model (PBM) using on-line flocculation data. The moving pivot discretisation technique is preferred to solve the PBM. A methodology for grid transformation and volume to number transformation is presented. Model fits on volume-based fitting variables fit the middle part of both the vol% and number distribution better, but under predict (30x) the smaller size classes. Model fits on number-based fitting variables fit the small size classes better, though still under predicting them (2x). For the application at hand, it is concluded that the model should be fitted to the number distribution. However, the improved methodology pointed out that the model lacks flexibility to adequately describe the data. Copyright © 2004 IFAC.

Model: Aggregation-breakage PBM
Laws:
(1) [balance] Tracks the floc-size distribution over time through size-space growth and aggregation and breakage source terms.
(2) [constitutive] Computes the net aggregation contribution from floc formation by collisions and loss of flocs through aggregation.
(3) [constitutive] Calculates the collision frequency between flocs from their volumes and the average velocity gradient.
(4) [constitutive] Calculates the average velocity gradient from turbulent energy dissipation and kinematic viscosity.
(5) [constitutive] Computes the net breakage contribution by adding fragments from larger flocs and subtracting flocs that break at size x.
(6) [constitutive] Calculates the breakage rate as a size-dependent power law.
(7) [definition] Calculates the mass mean diameter as the ratio of the fourth and third moments of the number-based size distribution.
(9) [definition] Calculates the cumulative number of flocs with size at least x at time t.

States (computed by the ODEs):
- n: Floc size distribution function
- x: Floc size, expressed as volume
- \dot{X}: Growth rate

Inputs (variables no law computes):
- x^{\prime}: Integration variable representing floc volume
- d: Differential element of the particle-size coordinate in the integrals.
- \varepsilon: Average turbulent energy dissipation rate.
- \Delta F_{N}: Increment in the number-based particle-size distribution used in the moment sums.
- x_{i}: diameter of size class i

Model-wide assumptions:
- No significant growth occurs during the short flocculation experiments.
- Binary breakage is assumed, so Γ equals 2.

Size-dependent floc breakage with binary fragmentation
answer.description: The model represents activated-sludge flocculation and predicts how the floc-size distribution changes over time under mixing. It balances aggregation from floc collisions against size-dependent breakage and its fragments, with collision frequency linked to turbulence; growth is assumed negligible and breakage is binary. It was calibrated against experimental floc-size distribution data from short flocculation experiments.
